s1.syndrome_frame: Ocular inflammation with eyelid involvement and conjunctival hyperemia in a patient with a history of inflammatory bowel disease
salient_findings: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous upper and lower eyelids
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
key_facts: Switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse
Crusty plaques on the eyelid margins
Rest of the ophthalmic examination was unremarkable

differentials: Tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitor-associated ocular inflammation
per_call: Tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitor-associated ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Blepharitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins

shortlist.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: History of Crohn disease and ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Infliximab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Initial treatment with infliximab and subsequent ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Switch to adalimumab due to disease relapse and ongoing ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Seborrheic dermatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids, which can be associated with seborrheic dermatitis

raw.rationale: The patient's eyelid symptoms appeared during TNF-α inhibitor treatment, which includes infliximab, and resolved after treatment discontinuation, suggesting a likely adverse reaction to the medication.

rejected.label: Blepharitis
rejected.why: While blepharitis could explain some symptoms, it doesn't account for the temporal relationship with TNF-α inhibitor treatment.

rejected.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
rejected.why: The patient's ocular symptoms seemed more directly related to the medication than to the Crohn disease itself.

rejected.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
rejected.why: The symptoms were present before the switch to adalimumab, suggesting infliximab as the more likely culprit.

rejected.label: Seborrheic dermatitis
rejected.why: While seborrheic dermatitis can cause similar skin symptoms, the specific context of TNF-α inhibitor treatment and the resolution after discontinuation points towards a drug-induced reaction rather than a separate dermatological condition.
